title: Tenant-aware synthetic-grade health probes for VPC control plane upgrades
creator: Aisha Mensah
description:
Problem: Current private control plane canary gating relies primarily on sampled production traffic and coarse downstream telemetry. This misses tenant-specific regressions (e.g., tenant A's long sequence distribution, tenant B's heavy reranking workloads) and late-breaking failure modes that only show under particular KV cache or batching patterns.

Goal: Build a tenant-aware synthetic probe harness that: (1) can instantiate ephemeral probe runners inside a customer's VPC via Terraform/IaC, (2) execute representative multi-tenant workload profiles (prompt shapes, streaming patterns, embedding workloads, and retry semantics), (3) emit structured telemetry aligned with our Canary controller, and (4) surface deterministic pass/fail signals and confidence intervals to gate control plane version promotions.

This ticket scopes the end-to-end design, Terraform module, probe controller integration, and the initial staging rollout for three pilot tenants. The outcome should reduce upgrade-related incidents caused by tenant-specific workload regressions and shorten verification time for private upgrades.
implementation_notes:
High level plan:
- Phase A: Design and validation (this ticket) — define tenant profile schema, telemetry contract, pass/fail logic, and IaC boundaries.
- Phase B: Terraform module and probe image — build 'vpc-probe-runner' terraform module and a lightweight probe container that supports load shaping, scripted prompts, and KV cache priming.
- Phase C: Canary controller integration — extend the canary controller to provision probes via Terraform, kick off workloads, aggregate telemetry, and compute verdicts using statistical tests (bootstrap confidence intervals).
- Phase D: Staging pilots and tuning — run against 3 pilot tenants, tune thresholds and time windows, codify runbook.

Trade-offs considered:
- Running synthetic probes in-customer VPC vs. synthetic traffic routed through our hosted infra: we choose in-VPC runners to capture networking and private endpoint behaviors but require stronger IaC hygiene and least-privilege IAM.
- Complexity of per-tenant profiles: start with 3 canonical profiles (short-chat, long-incontext, embedding-heavy) and iterate to full per-tenant parametrization later.
- Verdicts: start with conservative thresholds to avoid false positives; allow opt-in stricter gating for high-risk tenants.

Security & compliance notes: probe runners must support customer KMS for any secrets, require audit logging, and the Terraform module must document required IAM permissions. The release notes will include RBAC and data retention guarantees for probe telemetry.
metrics_and_thresholds:
Primary signals: 1) p95/generation-latency delta vs baseline < +25%; 2) error_rate < 0.5% absolute increase; 3) kv_cache_hit_ratio decrease < 5 percentage points; 4) model_variant_mismatch_rate < 0.2%; 5) GPU memory OOMs = 0 during probe window.
Sample size and window: aim for at least 200 synthetic requests per profile and a 10-minute steady-state window for computing p95. Use bootstrap for confidence intervals.
Alerting: fire if any primary signal crosses threshold AND confidence >= 90%.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for probe harness parsing and telemetry emission.
- Integration tests: terraform module deploys to a sandbox VPC automatically (CI job), probe runs and reports back.
- Controlled chaos: inject latency and fail RPCs in staging to validate probe sensitivity.
- Manual verification: run probe against a known-bad control plane version to assert the probe flags the regressions.
- Load safety: probe runner must enforce rate limits and backoff to avoid impact on tenant production services.

next_steps: 1) Resolve Terraform apply permission with cloud-plat and document required IAM roles; 2) Harden probe image with secrets handling and KMS support; 3) Wire probe outputs into canary controller verdict API; 4) Schedule pilot runs with 3 tenants in staging and capture results; 5) Prepare runbook and on-call alerts for production enablement.
notes_from_reviews: PM (Ravi) requested an opt-in strict mode per-tenant to allow aggressive gate behavior for regulated customers.
SRE (Leah) emphasized low blast radius: probe runners must be ephemeral and enforce per-run quotas; also requested audit events for each Terraform execution.
Security (Nina) asked for a clear KMS integration plan and for the terraform module to avoid broad IAM policies in examples.
